segments.text: You've heard that we clink glasses to slosh our drinks together and prove there's no poison. Nice story. Zero evidence.
Try it. A polite clink doesn't swap a single drop. And historians have never found an old source for the poison tale.
But the word toast? That part is real. In the {1600s,|sixteen hundreds,} people dropped a piece of spiced toasted bread into their wine or ale, for flavor.
Soon the person you drank to was called the toast, as if they flavored the drink. That's where the toast of the town comes from.
So why the clink? Nobody knows for sure. The favorite theory: a drink already pleases your eyes, your nose, your tongue and your hand. The clink adds your ears. All five senses.
Or maybe it's simpler. Glasses touching is the closest a whole table can get to a group hug.
So next time someone tells you the poison story, clink their glass, and tell them the real one.
